stem_text: A spring of unstretched length 𝑙 has a mass m with one end fixed to a rigid support. Assuming spring to be made of a uniform wire, the kinetic energy possessed by it if its free end is pulled with uniform velocity 𝑣 is :

candidate_solve.derivation: Element at distance y from fixed end has speed v(y) = v*(y/l). Element mass dm = (m/l)dy. Total kinetic energy KE = int_0^l (1/2)*dm*(v(y))^2 = (1/2)*(m/l)*(v^2/l^2) * int_0^l y^2 dy = (1/2)*(m*v^2 / l^3) * (l^3 / 3) = (1/6)*m*v^2.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Continuous mass integration under linear affine velocity profile v(y) = v*(y/l)

representation_translation.evidence: Setting up 1D continuum integral for kinetic energy over spring length

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Formulate differential mass element dm = (m/l)dy, express local speed, evaluate polynomial integral

algebra_computational_load.evidence: Definite integration of y^2 yielding l^3/3 and resulting 1/6 prefactor

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Avoiding trap of treating spring as point mass (1/2 mv^2) or average speed (1/8 mv^2)

demand_proposal.rationale: Applying continuum kinetic energy integration to distributed mass spring
